eventMetadata.context_description: Ensemble forecasts from the German Weather Service (DWD) and ECMWF currently anchor trader sentiment around a 29–30 °C peak for Munich on August 11, 2026, with the market pricing 31 °C highest at 61.5 % and 30 °C at 34 %. Light south-westerly flow combined with variable high-cloud cover is limiting daytime solar heating and preventing stronger boundary-layer mixing that could push readings higher. Official guidance shows afternoon maxima near 28–31 °C under these conditions, consistent with late-summer climatology for the region. Any late-model shifts in cloud timing or wind direction could adjust the final official reading at Munich Airport, but consensus remains tightly clustered and has changed little in recent runs.

The slightly elevated reading today reflects a temporary moderation ahead of an approaching strong cold front that is expected to deliver cooler, windier, and wetter conditions over the long weekend. Model guidance shows limited spread, with most ensemble members clustering the maximum between 19–21 °C and only small probabilities attached to outliers above 22 °C or below 19 °C. Official observations from the South African Weather Service will resolve the market once the day’s peak temperature is recorded.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 12 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/qingdao/ZSQD.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecast models from sources including AccuWeather and regional meteorological guidance point to a maximum temperature of 30–31°C in coastal Qingdao on August 12, 2026, shaped by persistent cloud cover, light northeasterly flow, and possible thundershowers that limit daytime heating. These conditions align with typical late-summer patterns moderated by the Yellow Sea’s marine influence, keeping values near or slightly above the August climatological average of roughly 29–30°C. Earlier August heat warnings across inland Shandong, with peaks above 35°C, have eased, reducing the chance of outlier warmth. Market-implied odds heavily favor 30–31°C outcomes because ensemble guidance shows limited day-to-day variability and no strong warming or cooling signals through the 48-hour window. Updated model runs and official Shandong Meteorological Observatory briefings expected later on August 11 will provide the final inputs for resolution.

Model consensus from AccuWeather and similar sources projects similar values for mid-month, with limited upside potential unless clearer skies develop.
